evidence.excerpt: UNICEF and Japan turned over 400 educational tablets to support at least 800 non-readers and struggling readers in Eastern Visayas as part of learning recovery efforts.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraph describing tablets and target learners
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The claim is concrete and specific, though it is a partner-supported intervention rather than a full-government outcome evaluation.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year learning-recovery context in July 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly relevant to Marcos-era education recovery because it sits within the national learning-recovery environment, but the source is not a direct Marcos order.
contrary_evidence: This is a localized partner intervention, not a nationwide Marcos policy result.
It shows need and response, not macro-level educational improvement.

evidence.claim: In Marcos's first 100 days, DBM said it approved billions in assistance for rice farmers, the most vulnerable households affected by inflation, calamity victims, commuters, and healthcare workers, including P5,000 subsidies for more than 1.5 million rice farmers.
evidence.title: DBM releases billions of pesos to aid rice farmers, vulnerable households, calamity victims, commuters, healthcare workers in the first 100 days of Marcos Jr Administration
evidence.excerpt: In Marcos's first 100 days, DBM said it approved billions in assistance for rice farmers, the most vulnerable households affected by inflation, calamity victims, commuters, and healthcare workers, including P5,000 subsidies for more than 1.5 million rice farmers.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and subsidy details in the release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official budget-management release is strong evidence for the program rollout and intended beneficiaries.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and Marcos's first 100 days in office.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Marcos administration because the release describes first-100-days policy execution under his presidency.
contrary_evidence: It is an administrative release, not an independent audit of effectiveness.
The aid is responsive relief, not structural poverty reduction by itself.

evidence.claim: Marcos pledged support for Typhoon Paeng victims, distributed financial aid through DSWD's AICS program, and said he wanted a long-term solution to the flooding problem.
evidence.title: PBBM vows full support to ‘Paeng’ victims; eyes long-term solution to Cavite flooding problem
evidence.excerpt: Marcos pledged support for Typhoon Paeng victims, distributed financial aid through DSWD's AICS program, and said he wanted a long-term solution to the flooding problem.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs on aid distribution and long-term flood solution
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government release is strong for the fact of the aid distribution and the president's stated response.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year disaster response in October 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos because he personally led the aid distribution and situation briefing.
contrary_evidence: It shows emergency response, not durable resilience outcomes.
The main evidence is the president's own account of the response.

evidence.claim: Marcos placed several regions under a state of calamity after Severe Tropical Storm Paeng, directing agencies to continue rescue, relief, rehabilitation, and price-control measures and to augment basic services in affected areas.
evidence.title: PBBM declares state of calamity in ‘Paeng’-hit regions
evidence.excerpt: Marcos placed several regions under a state of calamity after Severe Tropical Storm Paeng, directing agencies to continue rescue, relief, rehabilitation, and price-control measures and to augment basic services in affected areas.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential release is strong for the decision and its stated purpose.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year disaster-response decision in November 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos as head of state exercising calamity powers.
contrary_evidence: The declaration is a response measure, not proof of successful recovery.
Its effect depends on later implementation by agencies and LGUs.

evidence.claim: Marcos signed the 2023 national budget in December 2022 and identified education, public works, health, social welfare, agriculture, and transportation as the priority sectors of his administration's first national budget.
evidence.title: PBBM signs P5.2 trillion 2023 national budget
evidence.excerpt: Marcos signed the 2023 national budget in December 2022 and identified education, public works, health, social welfare, agriculture, and transportation as the priority sectors of his administration's first national budget.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs on the 2023 budget and priority sectors
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget-signing release is strong evidence for the administration's stated spending priorities and legislative support.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year action at the end of 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos because he signed and described the first budget of his administration.
contrary_evidence: Budget priority is not the same as actual service delivery.
Spending outcomes depend on execution and procurement after enactment.

evidence.claim: The FY 2022 budget, inherited by Marcos when he took office, gave the biggest allocations to education, health, and social welfare and funded health-insurance premiums for 13.2 million indigent families and 7.3 million senior citizens.
evidence.title: Recovery, Growth, and Sustainability Highlighted in the Signed FY 2022 National Budget
evidence.excerpt: The FY 2022 budget, inherited by Marcos when he took office, gave the biggest allocations to education, health, and social welfare and funded health-insurance premiums for 13.2 million indigent families and 7.3 million senior citizens.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official budget documentation is strong for the inherited baseline, though it predates Marcos's term.
evidence.period_fit: Inherited baseline relevant to the start of Marcos's 2022 term.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Inherited baseline only; this budget was signed before Marcos became president.
contrary_evidence: Because it predates Marcos, it cannot be counted as his own performance.
It shows starting conditions rather than ruler-specific delivery.

evidence.claim: Marcos repeated in his inaugural address the claim that he built the Ilocos Norte windmills, but PCIJ says the projects were built by private companies and had already been fact-checked repeatedly.
evidence.title: Inauguration 2022: Marcos repeats false claim on Ilocos windmills
evidence.excerpt: Marcos repeated in his inaugural address the claim that he built the Ilocos Norte windmills, but PCIJ says the projects were built by private companies and had already been fact-checked repeatedly.
evidence.source_locator: paragraphs 2-5 around the quoted line 'I built them'
evidence.source_confidence_reason: This is a contemporaneous fact-check of a specific public statement, with the underlying project ownership identified in the same report.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target period at the start of Marcos's presidency.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable: the false claim is Marcos's own statement in his inaugural address.
contrary_evidence: He may have intended the wording rhetorically, but the article treats it as a factual assertion.
A single false claim does not prove a broader pattern by itself.

evidence.claim: Marcos used his first SONA to call for proper tax administration, while PCIJ noted that his family’s unpaid estate taxes remained an obvious unresolved issue that complicated his fiscal message.
evidence.title: In SONA speech, Marcos family’s unpaid estate taxes is the elephant in the room
evidence.excerpt: Marcos used his first SONA to call for proper tax administration, while PCIJ noted that his family’s unpaid estate taxes remained an obvious unresolved issue that complicated his fiscal message.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary contemporaneous reporting on the speech and the family tax issue, with a clear personal/family nexus.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and tied to Marcos's first SONA on July 25, 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mixed but direct: Marcos was personally responsible for the public fiscal message, while the tax liability was a family-interest issue that shadowed that message.
contrary_evidence: This is a family tax dispute, not proof of personal embezzlement.
The article critiques omission and conflict rather than establishing a new legal finding.

evidence.claim: Marcos said his family had not been given a chance to respond in the estate-tax case, but the fact-check says that claim was false because court records show notices were served and the case later became final and executory.
evidence.title: Fact check: Marcos Jr. claims family 'wasn't given a chance to respond' to estate tax case
evidence.excerpt: Marcos said his family had not been given a chance to respond in the estate-tax case, but the fact-check says that claim was false because court records show notices were served and the case later became final and executory.
evidence.source_locator: claim/rating/facts sections and the quoted passage about notices and the Supreme Court record
evidence.source_confidence_reason: A direct fact-check tied to a specific statement, with the court-history correction spelled out in the article.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year, after a 2022 interview about the estate tax case.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable: it is Marcos's own statement being fact-checked.
contrary_evidence: This addresses one claim, not every argument he made about the tax case.
The fact-check does not prove intent to deceive in every forum.

evidence.claim: The article says Marcos's 2022 victory came after a broad online and offline campaign to whitewash family history, that he was the biggest beneficiary of disinformation, and that Twitter suspended hundreds of pro-Marcos accounts for spam and manipulation in January 2022.
evidence.title: Navigating malign influence campaigns in the Philippines: a guide for journalists and newsrooms
evidence.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
evidence.excerpt: The article says Marcos's 2022 victory came after a broad online and offline campaign to whitewash family history, that he was the biggest beneficiary of disinformation, and that Twitter suspended hundreds of pro-Marcos accounts for spam and manipulation in January 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters Institute is a strong research outlet, and the claim is supported by external studies and platform actions referenced in the text.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on the 2022 campaign environment; published in 2023 but explicitly about the 2022 election cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mixed: it speaks to Marcos's campaign ecosystem and benefit from disinformation, not proof he personally authored every tactic.
contrary_evidence: This is an ecosystem claim, not a direct finding that Marcos personally ran each operation.
The article relies on outside studies and platform enforcement rather than a courtroom finding.

evidence.claim: AFP said the viral posts portraying the Marcos family in a positive light and downplaying the dictatorship were misleading, and a researcher described them as Marcos propaganda lacking context.
evidence.title: Posts mislead on media coverage of revolution that ousted late Philippine dictator
evidence.excerpt: AFP said the viral posts portraying the Marcos family in a positive light and downplaying the dictatorship were misleading, and a researcher described them as Marcos propaganda lacking context.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: AFP fact-checking is strong for identifying the falsity and context of the viral material, though it remains an ecosystem-level rather than court-level finding.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 campaign year and targeted at the Marcos family narrative environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly indirect but relevant: the material concerns the family brand and campaign ecosystem, not a single presidential statement.
contrary_evidence: The article focuses on family-history propaganda rather than a specific act by Marcos Jr.
It does not establish legal culpability, only misleading propaganda patterns.

evidence.claim: Marcos planned to appoint his longtime chief of staff and campaign spokesperson Victor Rodriguez as executive secretary, and the article says Rodriguez was described as 'fiercely loyal' to Marcos.
evidence.title: Marcos campaign spokesman chosen as next executive secretary
evidence.excerpt: Marcos planned to appoint his longtime chief of staff and campaign spokesperson Victor Rodriguez as executive secretary, and the article says Rodriguez was described as 'fiercely loyal' to Marcos.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-sourced business reporting is strong for the appointment and the loyalty characterization quoted in the article.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-inauguration 2022 cabinet formation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable: Marcos chose a close campaign insider for a top executive post.
contrary_evidence: A loyal insider is not automatically a corrupt appointment, but it does raise patronage concerns.
The article does not prove misuse of office by itself.

evidence.claim: Marcos signaled continuity in economic policy by naming Benjamin Diokno as finance minister and Felipe Medalla as central bank governor, with the article describing this as a move toward familiar faces.
evidence.title: Philippines' Marcos signals continuity ahead with new economic team
evidence.excerpt: Marcos signaled continuity in economic policy by naming Benjamin Diokno as finance minister and Felipe Medalla as central bank governor, with the article describing this as a move toward familiar faces.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs on the new economic team and continuity signal
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is strong for the appointment facts and the continuity framing.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-inauguration 2022 cabinet formation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable: these are Marcos's own appointments and stated preference for continuity.
contrary_evidence: Continuity is not the same as reform or anti-corruption.
The appointments show competence signals more than probity by themselves.

evidence.claim: Arsenio Balisacan accepted Marcos's offer to become economic planning chief, and the Reuters report says political affiliation was not a factor in Marcos's selection criteria; Balisacan had previously led the same agency from 2012 to 2016.
evidence.title: Anti-trust chief to lead Philippines' economic planning agency
evidence.excerpt: Arsenio Balisacan accepted Marcos's offer to become economic planning chief, and the Reuters report says political affiliation was not a factor in Marcos's selection criteria; Balisacan had previously led the same agency from 2012 to 2016.
evidence.source_locator: article body paragraphs on the appointment and the quoted selection rationale
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is strong for the appointment details and the prior-service record.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-inauguration 2022 cabinet formation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos's cabinet choice, with the caveat that the article reports his stated nonpartisan criterion rather than independently proving it.
contrary_evidence: The selection criterion is self-reported by the incoming administration.
Competence is inferred from prior service and resume, not from the future outcome of policy.

evidence.claim: On his first day in office, Marcos led the oath-taking of Cabinet members and named key officials including Sara Duterte, Benjamin Diokno, Arsenio Balisacan, and Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin Remulla.
evidence.title: Marcos receives arrival honors at Malacañang Palace, leads oath-taking of Cabinet members
evidence.excerpt: On his first day in office, Marcos led the oath-taking of Cabinet members and named key officials including Sara Duterte, Benjamin Diokno, Arsenio Balisacan, and Justice Secretary Jesus Crispin Remulla.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The report is contemporaneous and concrete about the official appointments, though it mainly reports the names and offices rather than evaluating integrity.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year on June 30, 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable: these are Marcos's own inaugural appointments.
contrary_evidence: The article does not itself test whether the appointees later acted independently.
Some appointees are political allies, so the item is mixed rather than purely positive.

evidence.claim: Marcos appointed Bartolome Vicente Bacarro, Rodolfo Azurin Jr., and Medardo de Lemos to head the AFP, PNP, and NBI, and the article describes Bacarro and Azurin as long-serving officers with extensive field and command experience.
evidence.title: Marcos picks new AFP, PNP, NBI chiefs
evidence.excerpt: Marcos appointed Bartolome Vicente Bacarro, Rodolfo Azurin Jr., and Medardo de Lemos to head the AFP, PNP, and NBI, and the article describes Bacarro and Azurin as long-serving officers with extensive field and command experience.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting gives the appointment facts and biographical context, though it does not prove the appointments were chosen solely for merit.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year appointment action in August 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable: Marcos chose the heads of the country's top security and investigative bodies.
contrary_evidence: Security appointments can still be politically useful even when the appointees are experienced.
The article does not rule out patronage motives, but it does show professional credentials.

evidence.claim: Marcos picked Juan Ponce Enrile, Menardo Guevarra, and Jose Faustino Jr. for senior posts; the article says Guevarra was chosen for his sterling performance as a lawyer and Faustino had over 38 years of military service, while Enrile was a staunch Marcos supporter.
evidence.title: Enrile, Guevarra, Faustino picked to serve under Marcos admin
evidence.excerpt: Marcos picked Juan Ponce Enrile, Menardo Guevarra, and Jose Faustino Jr. for senior posts; the article says Guevarra was chosen for his sterling performance as a lawyer and Faustino had over 38 years of military service, while Enrile was a staunch Marcos supporter.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The report is detailed on the appointments and credentials, but it also shows a mixed pattern because one appointee is explicitly described as a supporter.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year cabinet formation in June 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable: Marcos selected these senior figures for his incoming administration.
contrary_evidence: The explicit mention of Enrile as a staunch supporter weakens the clean-competence reading.
The source is mixed rather than purely positive.

evidence.claim: Marcos designated retired Chief Justice Lucas Bersamin as Executive Secretary, replacing Vic Rodriguez.
evidence.title: Ex-Chief Justice Bersamin named Executive Secretary
evidence.excerpt: Marcos designated retired Chief Justice Lucas Bersamin as Executive Secretary, replacing Vic Rodriguez.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraph and appointment summary in the PNA report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The state news agency report is strong for the appointment fact and the office change.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year appointment action in September 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable: Marcos chose a former chief justice for the office.
contrary_evidence: This is a personnel move, not proof of sustained anti-patronage practice.
It may partly reflect damage control after earlier inner-circle friction.

evidence.claim: The first post-SONA economic briefing under Marcos set out a comprehensive 8-point socioeconomic agenda to respond to inflation and pandemic scarring, create quality and green jobs, and use a medium-term fiscal framework to support robust growth.
evidence.title: Post-SONA Economic Briefing
evidence.excerpt: The first post-SONA economic briefing under Marcos set out a comprehensive 8-point socioeconomic agenda to respond to inflation and pandemic scarring, create quality and green jobs, and use a medium-term fiscal framework to support robust growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government transcript with dated event record and direct statements by senior economic officials.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022, at the start of Marcos's administration.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos and his economic team; it shows stated priorities and intended policy conversion, not proven success.
contrary_evidence: This is a plan and briefing, not independent proof of execution or outcomes.

evidence.claim: Marcos presented the 8-point socioeconomic agenda as a near- and medium-term policy roadmap, said the administration would address inflation by boosting local food production and targeted support, and tied the program to poverty reduction and upper-middle-income status.
evidence.title: Road to progress: PBBM touts eight-point socio-economic agenda before US investors, biz leaders
evidence.excerpt: Marcos presented the 8-point socioeconomic agenda as a near- and medium-term policy roadmap, said the administration would address inflation by boosting local food production and targeted support, and tied the program to poverty reduction and upper-middle-income status.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential release with direct quotes and specific program targets, but still self-reporting.
evidence.period_fit: Within 2022 and directly tied to Marcos's first-year governing program.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos as a public statement of goals and priorities.
contrary_evidence: The source shows declared intent, not independently verified implementation.

evidence.claim: Marcos told foreign businesses that the Philippines had sound macro fundamentals and a favorable investment policy environment, and said his administration would pursue structural reforms and a more competitive business climate for high-value investment.
evidence.title: PBBM invites Singaporean firms to invest in PH; bares 8-point economic agenda
evidence.excerpt: Marcos told foreign businesses that the Philippines had sound macro fundamentals and a favorable investment policy environment, and said his administration would pursue structural reforms and a more competitive business climate for high-value investment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official announcement with a clear dated policy pitch to investors.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos and his administration's investment strategy.
contrary_evidence: This is advocacy language and does not by itself show reforms were implemented successfully.

evidence.claim: NEDA said social protection and human capital development would be top short-to-medium-term priorities, focusing on purchasing power, reducing COVID scarring, and supporting poor and marginalized sectors.
evidence.title: Social protection, human capital dev’t top priorities in PDP
evidence.excerpt: NEDA said social protection and human capital development would be top short-to-medium-term priorities, focusing on purchasing power, reducing COVID scarring, and supporting poor and marginalized sectors.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government newswire reporting a keynote by the NEDA secretary with concrete priority language and policy framing.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and part of the Marcos administration's planning cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Marcos through his chosen economic planning leadership and the administration's planning agenda.
contrary_evidence: This is a planning statement rather than an audit of delivery or outcomes.

evidence.claim: Economic managers presented the Marcos administration's agenda as aiming to cut poverty to 9 percent and reach upper-middle-income status by 2028, while discussing the medium-term fiscal framework and broader economic plans with IMF and World Bank audiences.
evidence.title: PH socioeconomic agenda presented at IMF, World Bank meeting
evidence.excerpt: Economic managers presented the Marcos administration's agenda as aiming to cut poverty to 9 percent and reach upper-middle-income status by 2028, while discussing the medium-term fiscal framework and broader economic plans with IMF and World Bank audiences.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government newswire with explicit numeric targets and a concrete external-facing presentation of the administration's plan.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos's economic team and the agenda he set or endorsed.
contrary_evidence: This documents targets and advocacy, not achievement.

evidence.claim: Marcos said the first priority was the economy and named Diokno, Medalla, Balisacan, Pascual, and Bonoan to key economic posts, framing the team as continuity for jobs, commodity prices, and streamlined government operations.
evidence.title: Marcos names more economic managers
evidence.excerpt: Marcos said the first priority was the economy and named Diokno, Medalla, Balisacan, Pascual, and Bonoan to key economic posts, framing the team as continuity for jobs, commodity prices, and streamlined government operations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent business press with named appointments, direct quotes, and personnel detail beyond official self-description.
evidence.period_fit: Immediately before Marcos took office in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos's selection of key implementers and economic managers.
contrary_evidence: Several appointees were continuity picks rather than obvious reform outsiders, so the competence signal is mixed rather than categorical.

evidence.claim: On his first day, Marcos led the oath-taking of Cabinet members and named key officials across finance, planning, justice, public works, labor, migration, trade, social welfare, tourism, communications, interior, transport, budget, agrarian reform, defense, security, legal counsel, the BSP, and presidential support offices.
evidence.title: Marcos receives arrival honors at Malacañang Palace, leads oath-taking of Cabinet members
evidence.excerpt: On his first day, Marcos led the oath-taking of Cabinet members and named key officials across finance, planning, justice, public works, labor, migration, trade, social welfare, tourism, communications, interior, transport, budget, agrarian reform, defense, security, legal counsel, the BSP, and presidential support offices.
evidence.source_locator: article body opening paragraph and cabinet list
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent outlet reporting a concrete, dated roster of the new administration's top staffing choices.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022, on inauguration day.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos as the appointing authority.
contrary_evidence: Appointment breadth alone does not prove that the team executed effectively.

evidence.claim: Marcos appointed new leaders of the AFP, PNP, and NBI and set a staged transition for the AFP chief, signaling active management of the security bureaucracy and law-enforcement chain of command.
evidence.title: Marcos picks new AFP, PNP, NBI chiefs
evidence.excerpt: Marcos appointed new leaders of the AFP, PNP, and NBI and set a staged transition for the AFP chief, signaling active management of the security bureaucracy and law-enforcement chain of command.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent reporting on concrete appointments and implementation timing.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos's executive appointment authority.
contrary_evidence: The source shows personnel control, not whether those chiefs improved performance.

evidence.claim: Marcos replaced resigned Executive Secretary Victor Rodriguez with Lucas Bersamin, who was sworn in before the 9th Cabinet meeting and began duties immediately.
evidence.title: Ex-Chief Justice Bersamin named Executive Secretary
evidence.excerpt: Marcos replaced resigned Executive Secretary Victor Rodriguez with Lucas Bersamin, who was sworn in before the 9th Cabinet meeting and began duties immediately.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government newswire with a precise appointment, swearing-in, and immediate assumption of duties.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos's ability to replace a core coordinator and reconfigure the center of the executive office.
contrary_evidence: This shows adaptation in staffing, but not whether the change corrected deeper coordination problems.

evidence.claim: DBM submitted the first full one-year Marcos budget, with priority sectors including education, infrastructure, health, agriculture, and social safety nets, and presented it as a transparent and timely roadmap for recovery and growth.
evidence.title: DBM submits proposed P5.268-T 2023 budget to Congress
evidence.excerpt: DBM submitted the first full one-year Marcos budget, with priority sectors including education, infrastructure, health, agriculture, and social safety nets, and presented it as a transparent and timely roadmap for recovery and growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government newswire with concrete budget allocations, priorities, and legislative timetable.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and for the incoming Marcos budget cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Marcos through the budget he ordered and the executive team he empowered.
contrary_evidence: Budget proposal and sectoral allocations do not guarantee downstream execution or impact.

evidence.claim: Within 100 days, the PinasLakas campaign had administered 3,456,132 first booster doses and vaccinated 47,803 senior citizens, with almost 73.3 million Filipinos fully vaccinated by Oct. 10, 2022.
evidence.title: PinasLakas administers 3.4M 1st booster dose in 100 days
evidence.excerpt: Within 100 days, the PinasLakas campaign had administered 3,456,132 first booster doses and vaccinated 47,803 senior citizens, with almost 73.3 million Filipinos fully vaccinated by Oct. 10, 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government newswire reports exact rollout figures and date-stamped accomplishments.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to Marcos's first 100 days.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial-to-strong: Marcos publicly directed the booster push, while DOH/DILG and local implementers executed the rollout.
contrary_evidence: This is rollout volume, not direct proof of health outcome gains or equity of coverage.

evidence.claim: DepEd said all public schools nationwide would be mandated to implement five days of in-person classes starting November 2, 2022, and that it would expedite review of blended learning to address learning issues.
evidence.title: On the issuance of an Amendatory DepEd Order to DO 34, s. 2022
evidence.excerpt: DepEd said all public schools nationwide would be mandated to implement five days of in-person classes starting November 2, 2022, and that it would expedite review of blended learning to address learning issues.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary agency statement with a dated national implementation directive and specific start date.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and the Marcos administration's school-reopening timetable.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: the order is issued by DepEd under Sara Duterte, so Marcos's attribution is through executive oversight and support rather than direct authorship.
contrary_evidence: The policy follows earlier pandemic reopening work and does not isolate Marcos-specific causation for learning outcomes.

evidence.claim: UNICEF reported that classes had moved to full face-to-face modality, around 94 percent of Filipinos were satisfied with school reopening, and DepEd was implementing the RAPID learning-recovery framework with staffing and literacy-assessment measures.
evidence.title: Full return to in-person classes another milestone in learning recovery
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF reported that classes had moved to full face-to-face modality, around 94 percent of Filipinos were satisfied with school reopening, and DepEd was implementing the RAPID learning-recovery framework with staffing and literacy-assessment measures.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent UN-agency reporting with a survey result and implementation detail, though partly reliant on partner framing.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: this reflects the Marcos administration's reopening environment, but the article also notes continuing constraints and broad partner support.
contrary_evidence: UNICEF simultaneously warned that vulnerable children still needed support and that many public schools lacked minimum WASH facilities.

evidence.claim: The Supreme Court summarized the Marcos estate-tax litigation and stated that notices of the deficiency tax assessments and later notices of levy were served on Imelda Marcos, Bongbong Marcos, and their counsel, undermining the later claim that the family was denied notice and a chance to respond.
evidence.title: G.R. No. 120880
evidence.excerpt: The Supreme Court summarized the Marcos estate-tax litigation and stated that notices of the deficiency tax assessments and later notices of levy were served on Imelda Marcos, Bongbong Marcos, and their counsel, undermining the later claim that the family was denied notice and a chance to respond.
evidence.source_locator: decision summary and factual recitation in the case digest
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary court decision with detailed factual findings, though the relevant facts predate 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 background used only to evaluate the truthfulness of Bongbong Marcos's 2022 estate-tax claim.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bongbong Marcos as the person whose campaign statement was checked against the court record.
contrary_evidence: This does not prove 2022 office misconduct; it only rebuts a specific claim about the estate-tax case.
